lead_headline: Lost Coffee opens sixth Colorado shop in Arvada — zero filings exceed $4M threshold as foreclosure pipeline cools

restaurant.blurb: 1 new lead today: Taco John's (Globeville) — closure confirmed from August 2024 after 20+ years at Logan St location.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications for the twelfth consecutive day as the state licensing blackout extends deeper into May with no communication on system restoration. The 7-day window holds at absolute zero versus last Tuesday's identical flatline, marking two full weeks since the April 29-30 surge dumped 2,144 renewals and collapsed the pipeline. No new filings, no status updates, no backend activity — the freeze persists across all license types with May's calendar completely dark. Backend reconciliation or batch processing delays appear systemic, not transactional, as Monday's workweek opens with no visibility into queue restoration timelines.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday (Instagram post on Colorado Blvd retail redevelopment) extends the Monday-morning lull, but the 7-day tally surges to 53 across 9 sources — up 23% from last week's 43 and 11% above the 30-day rolling average. Denver Post dominates with 18 mentions (34% share), followed by Instagram (14) and a mix of Facebook/X cross-posts. Real estate and development coverage anchors the week's pickup, with Google News RSS driving all 53 discoveries. Week-over-week momentum accelerates as outlets sustain elevated engagement heading into mid-May — the 53-mention floor now establishes a new weekly baseline 23% ahead of last Tuesday's 43-mention comparison point.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) nudges MTD to +12 (+1.1/day) while 90-day net holds at +134. Sunday delivered the week's cleanest conversion — single new subscriber, zero churn — following Saturday's identical pattern. This week's +2 net (15 new, 13 canceled) compresses sharply from last week's +5 (27 new, 22 canceled), with acquisition volumes down 44% (15 vs 27) even as cancellations improve 41% (13 vs 22). MTD's +1.1/day rate runs 15% below YTD's +1.3/day baseline, signaling tighter inbound flow replacing last week's high-volume churn model. The pattern shifts toward lower-velocity acquisition with retention stabilizing — weekend's back-to-back +1 days suggest steadier conversion rhythm despite compressed absolute counts.
